questions.q: What is the value of the 6 in 5,264?
questions.why: The 6 is in the tens place (5 thousands, 2 hundreds, 6 tens, 4 ones). 6 × 10 = 60. Value means a number, not just the digit.

questions.q: What digit is in the hundredths place of 6.184?
questions.why: Count right from the point: tenths (1), hundredths (8), thousandths (4). Answer with just the digit.

questions.q: What is the value of the 4 in 0.143?
questions.why: The 4 is the second digit after the point: hundredths. 4 × 0.01 = 0.04.

questions.q: Jordan says the value of the 6 in 0.462 is 0.6. What is the correct value?
questions.why: The 6 is in the hundredths place (4 tenths, 6 hundredths, 2 thousandths), so 6 × 0.01 = 0.06. Jordan used the tenths value.
2.874 = 2 + 0.8 + 0.07 + 0.004. The 8 is in the tenths place, so it is worth 0.8.
1/10 means divide by 10, so every digit moves one place right: 2,500 ÷ 10 = 250. The answer should be smaller.
The tenths digit is 3. Next door is 5, so round up to 8.4. Nearest tenth keeps only one decimal digit, so not 8.350.
The tenths digit is 9. Next door is 6, so the 9 goes up, which makes 10 tenths. That carries to 20.0 (20).

questions.q: Write this number in standard form: 4 tens + 3 tenths + 5 thousandths
questions.why: 4 tens = 40, 3 tenths = 0.3, 5 thousandths = 0.005. There is nothing in the hundredths place, so it gets a 0: 40.305.
